frase_gancho.texto: Before meeting the peoples of Mexico, the hall asks what all humans share.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: This hall begins with a simple idea: all human beings share a common origin. From there, it explains how our bodies changed, how we learned to make tools, and how languages and cultures emerged. It draws on four branches of study: physical anthropology, archaeology, linguistics, and ethnology. Here you will meet Lucy, a female of one of the oldest species in the human lineage. You will also see the re-creation of a burial from tens of thousands of years ago. And a wall of skulls that speaks of our differences and of what we have in common. After that come the first inhabitants of the Americas.
